chunks: I was present with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a man from the Kharijites entered upon him and said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you worship?' He said: 'Allah the Exalted.' He said: 'Have you seen Him?'

He said: 'Rather, the eyes do not see Him through direct beholding of sight, but the hearts see Him through the realities of faith. He cannot be known by analogy, nor grasped by the senses, nor likened to people. He is described through the verses [of the Quran], recognized through the signs. He is not unjust in His judgment. That is Allah — there is no god except Him.'
He (the narrator) said: The man left while saying: 'Allah knows best where He places His Message.' [6:124]

key_terms.التَّنْزِيه: Tanzih — the theological principle of God's absolute transcendence and incomparability
key_terms.الْحَوَاسّ: The senses — the five physical senses; insufficient for comprehending divine reality
key_terms.الْخَوَارِج: Kharijites — the earliest Islamic sect known for rigid literalism and rejection of Imam Ali's (AS) authority; in this context, an ideological opponent
key_terms.الْقِيَاس: Qiyas/analogy — logical comparison; rejected as a method for understanding God's nature in Shia kalam
key_terms.حَقَائِقُ الْإِيمَانِ: The realities of faith — spiritual perception through sincere belief as opposed to sensory experience
key_terms.مُشَاهَدَةُ الْأَبْصَارِ: Direct visual beholding — the physical act of seeing with the eyes; denied for God in Shia theology

ai.seo_question: Can God be seen with the eyes according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records an encounter between Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) and a Kharijite who challenged the Imam by asking what he worships and whether he has seen God. The Imam's response encapsulates the Shia theological doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih): God is beyond physical sight, beyond rational analogy, beyond sensory perception, and beyond comparison with created beings, yet He is known through the signs of revelation and recognized through His attributes. The Kharijite's departure while reciting Quran 6:124 ('Allah knows best where He places His Message') signifies his implicit acknowledgment of the Imam's superior knowledge and divinely-granted authority.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from his father who said, 
‘I was present with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and a man from the Kharijites came over to him<sup>asws</sup> and said to him, ‘O Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>! Which thing do you<sup>asws</sup> worship?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted’. He said, ‘Have you<sup>asws</sup> seen Him<sup>azwj</sup>?’

Heasws said: ‘But, the eyes cannot see Himazwj with the visualizing of the visions, but the hearts seen Himazwj by the realities of the Eman. Heazwj cannot be recognised by the analogies, nor can Heazwj be realised by the sensory perceptions, nor can Heazwj be resembled with the people. Heazwj is Described in the Verses (of the Quran), recognised by the Signs. Heazwj is not tyrannous in Hisazwj Judgments. That is Allahazwj. There is no god except Himazwj’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So the man went out and he was saying, ‘[6:124] Allah best knows where He Places His Message’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Ma‘bad from ‘Abdallah ibn Sinan from his father who has said the following. “I met Imam abu Ja‘far (a.s.) and at that time a man from the Khariji group came to see the Imam (a.s.) and asked, ‘O abu Ja‘far, who do you worship?’” The Imam replied, “I worship Allah, the Most High.” He then asked, “Have you seen Him?”

The Imam then said, “Eyes can not see Him in an eye-witnessing process but the hearts can see Him through the reality of faith. Allah can not be known by analogy or physical senses and He is not similar to people. He is mentioned in the verses of revelation. He is known from the signs. He does not do injustice in His judgments. Thus, is Allah besides Him there is no Allah.”
The narrator has said, “The man then left the Imam (a.s.) saying, “Allah knows best to who should He entrust His message to mankind.”
